transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m having a hard time keeping my mind on things long enough to finish them. Even important stuff at work—like tracing a client’s network issue—I’ll look up and realize I’ve been rereading the same log entries over and over and still don’t really know what they said.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless?

Yeah… pretty often. If I’m sitting with a client or in a chess meeting, my leg’s usually bouncing, or I’m clicking a pen. Sometimes I’ll just keep twisting a cable tie in my fingers until someone gives me that look.
When did you first notice these difficulties with focusing and restlessness?

Pretty early, I guess. My mother still brings it up—grade school report cards saying I was bright, but I wouldn’t stay in my seat, blurted out answers, and somehow lost homework even when I’d actually done it.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?

Yeah… I do. Mostly in technical conversations. If I think I know the answer, it kind of jumps out before the other person’s done. I’ll talk over them, or sometimes reach for the keyboard too soon. I know it’s rude. I just… do it anyway.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking, like grabbing something or doing something physical without considering the consequences?

I’m not sure. I mean… not usually in a physical way, I don’t think. I might be quick to do something before I’ve fully thought it through, but grabbing things or acting out like that… I haven’t really noticed.
Do you have trouble managing your emotions, like getting really upset or angry over small things?
I’m not sure. I mean, I get irritated like anyone, but I haven’t really tracked it as a problem. I don’t know that I’d say I get really angry over small things.
Do you have trouble organizing tasks and managing your time effectively?

Yes. That’s probably one of the bigger problems.

If I don’t have something external keeping me on track—like the old ticketing system or an escalation calendar—my day just turns into… piles of sticky notes, half-finished emails, chess club reminders, parts orders. And then I can’t really tell what needs to happen first until something is already overdue.
Do you often talk more than others in social situations?
I don’t know. I’m not usually the loudest person in the room. Maybe if it’s something technical or something I’m interested in, I can go on a bit, but I haven’t really noticed it as a regular thing.
Do you ever find yourself doing physical things on impulse, like grabbing something or jumping up from your seat, without thinking about it first?

Yeah… sometimes. It’s not so much grabbing things, but if I’m supposed to sit still and just listen, I get this feeling like I need to get up or go check something right then. Like there’s a motor running under my skin.
Do you have mood swings, where your mood changes quickly or unexpectedly?
I’m not sure. I mean, I get frustrated, sure, but I wouldn’t say my mood flips suddenly out of nowhere. At least… not that I’ve really noticed.
Do you have difficulty waiting for your turn in lines or when waiting for something?

Yeah… waiting is pretty hard for me. Like if I’m on hold with a vendor or sitting in a clinic waiting room, I get really restless. I’ll keep checking the time, sighing, and wanting to move things along before it’s really my turn.
Do you have intense emotional reactions to things that wouldn't normally bother other people?
I don’t know… not really. I can get irritated, but “intense” reactions, like over things most people would shrug off—I’m not sure I’d describe it that way.
Did your symptoms like difficulty focusing, restlessness, and impulsivity significantly improve or worsen at any point in your life?

Yeah… I’d say it got a lot worse after I was fired. That was about… almost two years ago, maybe a year and ten months. I lost the routines and systems that kept me on track, and since then it’s caused real problems.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for ADHD?
No… not officially. I haven’t really been treated for it before.
Have you experienced these difficulties with focusing, restlessness, and impulsivity consistently since childhood, or have they varied in intensity over the years?

I think it’s been there since I was a kid, just… not always the same level. My mother still jokes that my grade school report cards said I was bright, but I wouldn’t stay in my seat, blurted out answers, and lost homework even when I’d actually done it.
Have these difficulties with focusing, restlessness, and impulsivity caused problems in your relationships or at work?

Yeah. Mostly work, but it spills into home too. Since I lost the structure of my old job, people don’t really trust me to follow through like they used to. I’ve lost some freelance clients, and I missed out on a senior service-manager role… which was hard to admit.

And, you know, my wife and I have had to worry more about money because of it. It’s been… not great.
Would you say that your difficulties with restlessness and impulsivity, or your difficulties with focusing and completing tasks, cause you more problems in your daily life?

The focusing and finishing things, definitely. The restlessness is there, but what brings me in is… I just can’t keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore, even when it matters.

Like I’ll be tracing a client’s network problem, and ten minutes later I realize I’ve reread the same log entries three times and still don’t know what they say. That’s the part that’s really causing problems.
Would you describe your symptoms as causing significant distress or impairment in your daily life?

Yeah… I’d say it’s significant. I don’t really like saying that, but since losing the structure of my old job, my reputation has taken a hit. I’ve lost freelance clients, didn’t get a senior service-manager role, and at home my wife and I have had to worry about money more because people don’t trust me to follow through.
Do you ever find yourself becoming so focused on something that you tune out everything else and lose track of time?
I’m not sure. I mean… maybe sometimes, if I’m really into something, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed it as a big pattern. Usually it feels more like the opposite.
Have you ever been told that you have symptoms of ADHD, predominantly inattentive type, by a healthcare professional?
Not that I can remember, no. I mean, I’ve had people comment on focus and that kind of thing, but I don’t think a healthcare professional ever specifically told me that.
